explanation.en: foreach walks every element of any IEnumerable, here a list or array of names.
var declares a local whose type is inferred from the initializer; it is still statically typed as int.
yield return turns the method into an iterator: each value is produced only when the caller asks for the next one.

codeSnippet:
// read a file without blocking the thread
string text = ____ File.ReadAllTextAsync("notes.txt");

explanation.en: await suspends the method until the Task<string> completes and unwraps its result, freeing the thread meanwhile.

codeSnippet:
// keep only the adults
var adults = people.____(p => p.Age >= 18).ToList();

explanation.en: LINQ Where filters a sequence by a predicate; ToList materialises the result.
nameof(count) is the string "count", checked at compile time, so a rename updates it too.
A declaration pattern with is tests the type and, on success, assigns the cast value to c.

codeSnippet:
// immutable type with value equality, in one line
public ____ Point(int X, int Y);

explanation.en: A positional record generates init-only properties, a constructor, Deconstruct and value-based Equals and ToString.
A using declaration calls Dispose when the enclosing scope ends, releasing the file handle.
A readonly field can be assigned only in its declaration or a constructor; later writes are compile errors.

codeSnippet:
// the last element of an array
int last = arr[arr.____ - 1];

explanation.en: Arrays expose their size as Length; the last valid index is Length - 1 (or arr[^1]).

codeSnippet:
var list = new List<int> { 4, 8, 15 };
Console.WriteLine(list.____); // 3

explanation.en: List<T> exposes its size as the Count property. Arrays use Length instead.

codeSnippet:
// ["a", "b", "c"] -> "a, b, c"
string line = ____(", ", items);

explanation.en: string.Join puts the separator between elements, never at the ends.
TryParse returns success as a bool and writes the number through an out parameter, declared inline here.

codeSnippet:
// the caller's variable is read AND updated in place
static void Bump(____ int counter) => counter++;

explanation.en: ref passes the variable itself, so the increment is visible to the caller. out would not compile: it cannot be read before it is assigned.

codeSnippet:
// accept any number of arguments: Sum(1, 2, 3)
static int Sum(____ int[] values) => values.Sum();

explanation.en: params lets callers pass a comma-separated list, which the compiler packs into the array.

codeSnippet:
// expression-bodied method
static int Square(int x) ____ x * x;

explanation.en: An expression body (=>) replaces a block that contains a single return statement.

codeSnippet:
// fall back to "guest" when name is null
string shown = name ____ "guest";

explanation.en: The null-coalescing operator ?? returns its left operand unless it is null, otherwise the right one.
A switch expression puts the value first, then arms of pattern => result; _ is the catch-all.
A static member belongs to the type itself, so it is called on the class name with no object.
override replaces a virtual or abstract base member, so calls through an Animal reference run Cat's version.
An interface declares members that implementing classes and structs must provide.

codeSnippet:
// sort people by age, youngest first
var sorted = people.____(p => p.Age).ToList();

explanation.en: OrderBy sorts ascending by the selected key (OrderByDescending sorts the other way). It is a stable sort.
TryGetValue returns whether the key exists and writes the value through out, all in one lookup.

codeSnippet:
// print a line to the terminal
____("Hello, world!");

explanation.en: Console.WriteLine writes the text followed by a newline to standard output.
